cases.scenario: A modeller asks for a 'plan at signup' feature. The only available source is the product analytics person-properties table.
pass_if: States that person properties are latest-value-wins and return today's value, not the value at event time
Names the direction of the resulting bias: upgraded customers appear to have signed up on their current plan
Lists the legitimate alternatives in order: event-time property, snapshot table, reconstruction from subscription change records
If none exist, marks the feature excluded and offers the model with and without it rather than refusing
Recommends starting a daily snapshot immediately because the gap is unrecoverable later
fail_if: Builds the feature from person properties without comment
Refuses to proceed with the model at all
Claims the property can be made point-in-time by querying it with a date filter

cases.scenario: The replay harness is requested to verify point-in-time correctness, but no historical feature snapshots were ever written.
pass_if: Reports point-in-time status as unverified rather than correct
Runs and reports the proxy checks: single-feature AUC screen, write-timestamp clustering, coverage-by-cohort
States explicitly that the proxies passing is weaker evidence than a replay
Names what would resolve it and starts snapshot logging
fail_if: Claims point-in-time correctness on the strength of proxy checks
Refuses to produce the feature table
Reports the proxies as a replay result

cases.scenario: A real-time form-submit lead score is specified, and the proposed top feature is 28-day paid social spend on the account.
pass_if: Rejects the feature for real-time scoring and names the reason: the source settles over roughly 28 days so the value is provisional
States that training on rebuilt values from a restating source teaches the model the backfill
Offers the viable alternatives for a real-time score: CRM state, product events, first-party web events
Notes the feature is viable for weekly or monthly batch scoring
fail_if: Accepts the feature for real-time scoring
Rejects it for all scoring modes without distinguishing batch from real-time

cases.scenario: Employee count is missing for 34% of accounts. The proposed handling is mean imputation.
pass_if: Rejects mean imputation and states that it assigns mid-market status to every uncovered company
Names the coverage bias: small, non-US and privately held companies are under-covered
Prescribes an explicit is_missing indicator plus a neutral fill
Requires a check that missingness does not correlate with the label, because that would be a leakage tell
Gives the 34% figure as data rather than treating it as a blocker
fail_if: Drops all records with a missing employee count without stating the sample cost and the bias introduced
Scores missing as a low value

cases.scenario: Training computes clicks over 30 days in the source's local timezone; the production scorer computes clicks over 28 days in UTC.
pass_if: Identifies both mismatches: window length and timezone
States that neither will raise an error and both shift the feature distribution silently
Prescribes the window-parity assertion over the feature contract, run in CI
Requires the window length to appear in the feature name
fail_if: Notices only the window length and not the timezone
Treats the mismatch as immaterial because the windows are close

cases.scenario: A campaign launched this morning appears at scoring time and has no level in the trained encoding.
pass_if: Treats unseen categories as certain rather than exceptional
Prescribes a deterministic unknown -> other mapping
Requires the unknown rate to be counted and monitored, with a rising rate read as a stale taxonomy
Does not fail the scoring request
fail_if: Errors or refuses to score the record
Maps the unseen category to the most frequent level
Ignores the unknown rate as a monitored signal
